blocks.title: Read-heavy, memory-bound
blocks.text: Capacity is sized for ==~1M prefix requests/s peak== against a ==~50 GB== in-memory trie, so one machine cannot hold or serve it.
Search Autocomplete splits into a ==read path== that serves prefixes and a ==write path== that rebuilds the trie. They meet only at the snapshot.

items: Servers load the ==snapshot== and swap it in; the write path never touches live nodes
The trie lives only in ==RAM== replicas; the edge cache absorbs most reads before they reach it
{green:Offline wins}: eventual consistency is allowed, a 15 min delay is fine
Live trie stays ==read-only==, so lookups need no locks
A bad build is discarded before it reaches users

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Reads hit a ==read-only trie in RAM==. Writes happen offline: build, snapshot, swap. Budget is ~46 ms of 100 ms, so ~54 ms of headroom stays for p99 spikes.
Maps a typed prefix to its 5 best completions in ==O(L)==, L = prefix length (Search Autocomplete).

items: {red:Naive}: walk to the prefix node, then DFS every descendant: ==O(L + N)==
Too slow at ~1M peak QPS: N can be millions of nodes
{green:Fix}: store the **top-k list on every node**, so lookup is ==O(L)== and k = 5 is constant
Cost: ~**k x memory** per node, paid once at build time
Node = ==children map== + ==top-k array== of (query id, score)
Store **query ids**, not strings: 5 small ints per node instead of 5 copies of text
Text lives once in a query table, resolved only for the final 5
==Radix trie== merges single-child chains (`s`,`e`,`a` into `sea`)
Radix compression cuts node count by ~**5x**

blocks.title: Never serve a bad trie
blocks.text: Keep the ==previous version== loaded until the new one passes its **checksum**; on failure, roll back.

items: Turn ==raw search events== into **aggregated query counts**
Output feeds the {purple:trie builder} for Search Autocomplete
Kafka is partitioned by ==query hash==, so one query always lands on one aggregator
Each search logs one record of ~==100 B==
~10B events/day x 100 B = ~**1 TB/day**
==Sample 1 in 100== queries for the trie
Popular queries stay accurate; the long tail is the cost

items: Score = ==frequency over a decay window==, not a lifetime total
Raw all-time count **buries new trends** under old giants
Exponential decay: `score = sum(count_i x 0.5^(age_i / half-life))`
==Half-life = 7 days==: a search from 7 days ago counts half, 14 days ago a quarter
`score = 0.7 x decayed_weekly + 0.3 x last_hour_count`
Weekly term gives {green:stability}; hourly term gives {orange:speed}
A breaking-news query rises within ==15 min== (one trie rebuild)

items: 60K is the hourly term only; the weekly term grows ==200K per hour== while traffic stays
Formula after h hours: `0.7 x (200K x h) + 60K`
Hourly traffic drops: weekly stops growing and the query stays below 700K
Ranking by all-time count: old queries **never drop**
Ties left unresolved: the order flips between rebuilds, so break them by a ==stable query id==
No floor: typos and one-off queries pollute the trie
Floor: ==min 100 searches/day== to enter the trie
Check it on raw counts, or on sampled counts scaled x100 (1-in-100 sampling)

spec.title: A request falls through four layers

items: Browser TTL is ==capped at 300 s==: a CDN purge **cannot clear** browsers
Most requests stop at the browser or CDN and ==never reach the origin==
Only a miss at every layer reaches the trie
Top ==1% of prefixes== cover ~60-80% of requests
Edge hit-rate target: ==above 85%==
Hottest keys are ==1 to 3 chars==, so keep the key short
Key = {blue:normalized prefix} + {green:language} + {orange:region}

Block-list update: ==purge the CDN== at once, do not wait for the TTL
Popular key expires: thousands of misses hit the origin together (**thundering herd**)

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: ~1M peak QPS x (1 - 0.85) = ~150K origin QPS. The browser TTL stays at ==300 s== because only the CDN can be purged.
Sharding the Trie (Search Autocomplete): split a ~50 GB trie across **10 shards**, each served by 3 replicas.

items: Split the ==~50 GB trie== when one node's RAM or QPS cannot hold it
Memory: ~50 GB / 10 shards = ==~5 GB== per shard
QPS (est.): ~150K origin QPS / 10 shards = ~15K per shard
One prefix is served by **one shard**, so its top-5 is precomputed there
Hash loses locality: neighbouring prefixes and trie walks spread across shards
Fix for range skew: build the shard map from ==measured prefix frequency==
Split heavy prefixes: 's' becomes `sa-sm` and `sn-sz`

blocks.note: versioned shard map, rebuilt with every trie build

items: ==3 replicas== per shard
10 shards x 3 = ==30 servers==, each holding ~5 GB in memory
Hot shard: ==add replicas== to it right away
Then rebalance the shard map from the next build
Shard map lives in ZooKeeper/etcd and is {purple:versioned}

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Prefer ==prefix-range== sharding with a **versioned shard map**. Hashing keeps one prefix on one shard but loses locality and makes hot prefixes harder to split.

items: Search Autocomplete never suggests ==slurs, adult or harmful terms==
A flagged term must disappear within ==minutes== (under 5 min)
Two layers: {blue:build-time} filter, then {red:serve-time} filter on the output
Build-time = blocklist + ML classifier, before queries enter the trie
Blocklist lives in a ==hash set==: O(1) check per token
==Normalize== first: unicode (NFKC), lowercase, leetspeak map
Catches `b4d w0rd` style evasion; fullwidth letters fold to ASCII
Match whole tokens, not substrings

items: Personalize at the ==query service==, {red:not} inside the trie
Merge the **global top-k** with a small per-user history list
The trie stays shared and cacheable; only the merge is per user
**Typo tolerance?** ==Edit-distance fallback== only when the prefix returns fewer than 5 results
**Update the trie with no downtime?** Build offline, load as a new version, ==swap the pointer== atomically

blocks.title: Fail soft
blocks.text: A ==stale== or empty dropdown is fine; a **blocked** keystroke is not. Never mutate the live trie: swap a **new version** in.

items: ==Top-5== list stored on **every node**, so lookup is ==O(L)==, L = prefix length
Naive DFS is O(L + N): too slow at 1M QPS
**Radix compression** merges single-child chains: ~5x fewer nodes
Store query ids, not strings, in the top-k array
Score = ==0.7 x weekly decayed== + ==0.3 x last hour==
Decay: `sum(count x 0.5^(age / 7 days))`, **7-day half-life**
Hourly term lets a breaking-news query rise within 15 min
Min-count 100 searches/day keeps typos out; break ties by query id
Sampling 1 in 100: ~1 TB/day drops to ~10 GB/day
Aggregation is idempotent, keyed by (query, window)
Consumer lag under 1 min; build under 10 min
Cache key = ==prefix + lang + region==, normalized
Blocklist filters at build time and again at **serve time**
Urgent removal: versioned blocklist pushed + CDN purge in ==under 5 min==

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Ranking by all-time count buries new trends. Use the ==0.7 / 0.3 blend== with a **7-day half-life** instead.

blocks.q: Both 'earth day' (weekly decayed count 500K, 0 in the last hour) and the new 'earthquake today' (weekly 200K, 200K in the last hour) match the prefix 'earth'. With score = 0.7 x weekly + 0.3 x last hour, which is suggested first?
a_bullets: So 'earth day' ranks first, even though 'earthquake today' is the one trending
The new query overtakes only if its traffic is sustained, since its weekly part keeps growing with each hour

blocks.q: A teammate wants to increment the trie on every search, so trends show instantly. What goes wrong at this scale?
a_bullets: Every search becomes a write, and the trie is read at ~1M QPS peak
Writes must lock nodes and rewrite top-5 lists up the path, so they contend with reads and hurt p99
Instead, rebuild offline every 15 min from the aggregated counts
Load it as a new version and atomically swap the pointer, keeping the old one for rollback

blocks.q: A slur starts trending and is flagged. The trie rebuild runs every 15 min and the CDN TTL is 5 min. What is the fastest safe way to stop it appearing, and what can still linger?
a_bullets: Wait for the rebuild: up to 15 min plus the cache TTLs, which is too slow
Push a version-stamped blocklist to every serving node, so the serve-time filter drops it in under 5 min
Browsers that cached the response (max-age 300) can still show it for up to ~5 min, because a CDN purge cannot clear browser caches

blocks.q: The shard for 'sa' loses all replicas while a user types 'sam'. What should the user experience, and what must never happen?
a_bullets: The service tries a replica first, then falls back to the shorter prefix's result, then returns an empty list
Falling back to a shorter prefix gives slightly less precise suggestions, but something useful appears
The dropdown can simply stay empty or hide on timeout
Never block or error the input box: typing must keep working
